entities.label: AgentObligationBinding
entities.rationale: An agent-obligation binding is a normative tie that attaches a legal obligation to a specific agent. In BFO terms, it is externally grounded (arising from legal or social context, not intrinsic properties of the agent), inheres in the agent-bearer, and qualifies the agent as one who is bound. This matches BFO Role (BFO_0000023): an externally conferred, specifically dependent continuant. It is distinct from LegalObligation (the obligation itself, already in the ontology as a Role/SDC) in that it specifically denotes the binding relationship as a role the agent bears. Alternatively it could be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) if framed as an internal capacity to be compelled, but the external grounding of legal obligation better fits Role. A new class is proposed since no existing class captures the agent-side binding relation specifically.

relations.rationale: AgentObligationBinding is a subclass of Role (BFO_0000023) because it is an externally grounded specifically dependent continuant inhering in an agent-bearer.

An agent-obligation binding is a species of LegalObligation: it is the role of being bound by a legal obligation, making it a subclass of the existing LegalObligation role class. This captures that the binding is a legal-obligation-type role specifically indexed to an agent.

open_questions: Should AgentObligationBinding be a subclass of LegalObligation, or should it be a separate sibling class under BFO_0000023 that stands in a relational property to LegalObligation? The two interpretations differ: subclass means every agent-obligation binding is a legal obligation; sibling means it is a distinct role triggered by a legal obligation.

Is 'agent-obligation binding' intended to capture the obligation as it inheres in a particular agent (i.e., a specific role token), or the general structural relation between agents and obligations (which might better be modeled as an OWL property or a relational quality)?

Should the binding be modeled as a Disposition (BFO_0000016) rather than a Role (BFO_0000023), if the intent is to capture the agent's internal susceptibility to normative compulsion rather than an externally assigned status?
proposal.rationale_summary: The phrase 'agent-obligation binding' denotes the normative attachment of a legal obligation to a specific agent — i.e., what it means for an agent to be the bearer of an obligation. In BFO 2020, this is best classified as a Role (BFO_0000023): it is a specifically dependent continuant that inheres in the agent-bearer, is externally grounded in legal/social context rather than in the agent's intrinsic properties, and is realized in the agent's legally compliant or non-compliant behavior (processes). The existing class LegalObligation is already typed as BFO_0000023 (Role), so AgentObligationBinding is proposed as a subclass of LegalObligation — capturing that this is the obligation role as it specifically binds an individual agent. Key open questions concern whether subclassing LegalObligation is the right structural move, whether the concept is better modeled as a Disposition, or whether it should be represented as a relation (OWL object property) between an agent and an obligation instance rather than as a class.
